topStories.headline: Crash Sends SUV Into Jolene's, Leaving Mission Queer Bar With $10,000 Repair Bill
topStories.dek: A two-car collision at 16th and Harrison streets on Monday morning drove an SUV backwards through the front gates of the seven-year-old bar, injuring the driver and forcing the owner to launch a fundraiser.
topStories.body:
A two-car crash shortly before 8 a.m. on October 13 sent an SUV hurtling backwards into the entry gates and front door of Jolene's, the queer bar at the corner of 16th and Harrison streets in the Mission District. A pickup truck and an SUV collided at the four-way intersection; the SUV's airbags deployed on impact and the vehicle came to rest embedded in the bar's front entryway, according to Mission Local and SFist.

The female driver of the SUV was taken away by ambulance on a stretcher. The male driver of the pickup truck appeared unharmed. Workers at nearby businesses reported hearing a loud crash but only saw the aftermath, as their storefronts face away from the intersection.

Owner Jolene Linsangan arrived at the bar around 12:30 p.m. after being alerted by a neighbor. The lefthand entryway's lower portion was smashed in, exposing a wooden beam, and the iron security gate was bent inward — though it appears to have prevented the vehicle from reaching the interior doors. Linsangan told Mission Local she estimates repairs at roughly $10,000, money she will likely have to advance out of pocket while an insurance claim remains pending.

To cover immediate costs, Jolene's launched a fundraiser on the day of the crash, selling $20 tickets redeemable at any future event with a cover charge of $20 or less. Linsangan said she planned to open as usual on Thursday, keeping the bar's regular Thursday-through-Saturday schedule intact. Jolene's opened in early 2019 and is one of San Francisco's few dedicated lesbian and queer bar spaces.

topStories.headline: Who Gets the Mission's $743,000? Arts Commission Opens Bidding After MCCLA Closure
topStories.dek: Nine months after the Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts shut its doors, the city says it will begin accepting applications for the funds it held for the nearly 50-year-old institution — while the center itself hunts for a new temporary home.
topStories.body:
The city of San Francisco is sitting on $743,000 in arts and cultural programming funds intended for the Mission District, and it will soon open that money to competitive bids. Denise Pate, director of community investment at the San Francisco Arts Commission, told Mission residents at a community meeting on October 14 that applications will be accepted later this year, following the abrupt closure of the Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts (MCCLA) in January.

The nearly 50-year-old center closed permanently on January 28, 2026, after running out of funds — an outcome months in the making after staff layoffs, leadership turnover, and a city decision not to advance a scheduled grant payment. After it closed, MCCLA partnered with The San Francisco Study Center as a fiscal sponsor, the same organization that backstops Calle 24, the nonprofit overseeing the Calle 24 Latino cultural district on 24th Street. The city approved a separate $122,500 grant in April to fund the storage of the center's archive.

The Arts Commission said the San Francisco Study Center can apply for the main programming funds on MCCLA's behalf, but all applicants — including other Mission arts organizations — will be eligible to compete. Pate said proposals must demonstrate a clear, sustainable plan for ongoing programs. Meanwhile, board member Rob Sanchez said the center has narrowed its search to three possible temporary locations; which one is selected will depend on securing city funding.

The MCCLA building at 2868 Mission Street, a city-owned property the center leased for a dollar a year, is slated for seismic retrofitting. The building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is a San Francisco Designated Landmark.

topStories.headline: A Parking Lot Between 16th and 17th Will Become 152 Apartments — One of the First Mission Towers to Break Ground in Years
topStories.dek: Developers DM Development and Ascentris have secured a $61.7 million construction loan and plan to break ground in November on a nine-story building at 321 Florida Street, only the second market-rate apartment project of its size to start in San Francisco since 2023.
topStories.body:
A half-acre surface parking lot on Florida Street between 16th and 17th streets in the Mission District is set to become a nine-story, 152-unit apartment building, with groundbreaking scheduled for November 2026. Developer DM Development and Denver-based investment firm Ascentris announced the closing of the property in September, backed by a $61.7 million construction loan from PNC Bank — the two companies' first joint venture together.

The project at 321 Florida Street is expected to be only the second market-rate multifamily building with more than 28 units to break ground in San Francisco since 2023 — a signal of what observers are calling a modest thaw in a years-long construction freeze driven by high interest rates, elevated costs, and a sluggish permitting environment. City officials first approved housing on the parking lot site back in 2021.

Of the 152 planned units — a mix of studios, one-bedrooms, and two-bedrooms — 15 will be affordable, ranging from very-low-income to moderate-income households, a threshold that qualified the project for the state density bonus. The building will also include 39 covered parking spaces and approximately 10,000 square feet of indoor-outdoor rooftop amenity space, including a resident lounge, fitness center, and a terrace deck with views of the city skyline and the Bay. Construction is expected to wrap in late 2028.

events.title: Film Screening: 'Prodigal Daughter' with Director Q&A — Bernal Heights Library
events.location: Bernal Heights Branch Library, 500 Cortland Avenue
events.description: A screening of Prodigal Daughter — director Mabel Valdiviezo's documentary about reuniting with her family in Peru after 16 years and navigating her past as an undocumented immigrant in the U.S. — followed by a live Q&A with the director. Free and open to the public.

events.title: Mission Bernal Neighborhood Cleanup

events.title: Alemany Farm 21st Annual Harvest Festival
events.description: The largest agricultural site in San Francisco hosts its free annual fall celebration with garlic planting, farm tours, live music, a pig roast, farm salad, grilled items, family activities, and community groups. Donations welcome; very limited on-site parking.

events.title: Lit Crawl SF 2026 — Litquake's Free Literary Pub Crawl Through the Mission
events.location: Mission District — multiple venues along Mission, Valencia, and 24th streets
events.description: The annual cap to the Litquake festival brings 250-plus authors to 50-plus events spread across Mission bars, cafes, bookshops, and storefronts in three timed phases from 5–9 p.m. Free, with a $10–$15 suggested donation; afterparty follows at The Drawing Room Annex.

moreNews.headline: SF School Educators Are Accompanying Immigrant Families to ICE Appointments — 137 Families Helped, None Arrested
moreNews.body: Since January 2026, educators and volunteers trained through a collaboration between San Francisco Unified School District, a nonprofit, and the teachers' union have accompanied 137 SFUSD families to immigration appointments and court hearings, Mission Local reported on October 15. Educators in 20 schools across the district have received this training — a program with particular relevance in Mission District schools, where many students come from immigrant households facing federal immigration enforcement. None of the families accompanied by school staff have been arrested at their appointments so far.
